newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in lacklustre trade on Tuesday with most traders sidelined ahead of the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later tonight, dealers said.
The FOMC meets amid market speculation the central bank is poised to hike short-term interest rates by 0.25 percentage points to put the brakes on inflation.
But traders said it would take a 0.50-percentage point rise in the Federal Funds rate to move the dollar higher, while keeping interest rates unchanged could push the U.S. unit lower.
"All eyes are on what the Federal Reserve policy makers plan to do with monetary policy at tonight's meeting. There's nothing much to do, so everyone is waiting," a local dealer said.

"The market is expecting a 25-basis-point hike, but it has already been built into the market, so I don't think there will be much impact. We will just have to wait and see what happens after the meeting," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday, Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Monday's 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2, six-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/8 6 percent.
